sets.relationshipLabel: raw material converted by a process into a building material
sets.explanation: Clay is fired into brick and sand is melted into glass — each pair is a raw material transformed by heat into something structural.

sets.relationshipLabel: a tradesperson and the tool of their trade
sets.explanation: A mason reaches for a trowel and a carpenter for a chisel — each trade is defined by the tool that does its signature work.

sets.relationshipLabel: a structural element and the feature it always has
sets.explanation: Every column has a capital and every vault has a keystone — the named part is a fixed, defining feature of the structure.

sets.relationshipLabel: the ceremony or moment that opens a project and the one that closes it
sets.explanation: Excavation and cornerstone-laying begin a project just as occupancy and ribbon-cutting close it out — one marks the start, the other the finish, at different scales of ceremony.
